title: The Folding Mechanism
teaches: Definition of a brisk fold: pairing first/last, second/second-to-last, etc., and summing them.
visual: A list [1, 2, 3, 4] appears. Arrows connect index 0 to 3 (1+4) and index 1 to 2 (2+3). The numbers collapse into two new blocks: [5, 5].
narration: A brisk fold pairs the first element with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and sums each pair. For even-length lists, every number finds a partner; for odd-length lists, the middle element remains unpaired at the end.

title: Odd-Length Edge Case
teaches: Handling of the middle element in odd-length lists during a brisk fold.
visual: List [1, 2, 3] appears. Arrows connect 1+3=4. The '2' slides alone to the right end. Result: [4, 2]. Label 'Middle stays' highlights the unpaired element.
narration: When the list has odd length, all elements except the exact middle one are paired and summed. The middle number does not fold; it simply moves to the end of the new list as a standalone value.

title: Rule 2: Length Reduction
teaches: The structural change: length roughly halves after one brisk fold.
visual: List [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] (length 6) folds to [7, 7, 7] (length 3). An arrow labeled 'Length / 2' connects the two states. Visual emphasis on the halving effect.
narration: Each brisk fold roughly halves the length of the list. This compression property makes brisk folds useful for reducing data size while maintaining its essential numerical sum.
